cards.text: Paul, the apostle who wrote this letter to the Galatians (Galatians 1:1), is wrapping it up. Now he picks up the pen and writes with his own hand. I don't know about you, friend, but when somebody writes it BY HAND, I'm reading every word.

cards.question: Paul tells the Galatians to look at how tiny his handwriting is.

cards.text: Then Paul calls out some people who want to make a good impression on the outside, and they're trying to compel the Galatians to be circumcised. All sprinkles, no cookie.

cards.question: Paul says these people push circumcision to keep themselves safe. Safe from what?

answers.text: Persecution for the cross of Christ
Being put out of the synagogue

cards.question: Paul says the people pushing circumcision keep the law themselves.
These people don't keep the law, yet they still want the Galatians circumcised so they have something to boast in. What is it?

cards.text: Those people want to boast, but Paul flips it: "But as for me…" Friend, I'd brag about one perfect batch for a WEEK straight, and Paul's only got one thing he'll boast in.

cards.question: Paul says he'll never boast, except in the ___ of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Through the cross of Christ, what does Paul say has happened between him and the world?

answers.text: The world has been crucified to him and he to the world
The world has made peace with him and he with the world
The world has forgotten him and he has forgotten the world

cards.text: Then Paul takes the whole circumcision question and settles it in one line. Mic drop, friend, or I guess PEN drop.

cards.question: Paul says being uncircumcised is what really counts.
Neither circumcision nor uncircumcision means anything, Paul says. What counts is a new ___.

cards.text: After all this pressure over circumcision, Paul turns to the ones who walk by this rule. And he's got a blessing for every single one of them.

cards.question: What blessing does Paul wish on all who walk by this rule?

cards.text: And Paul keeps that peace and mercy going: "even to the Israel of God." He's like me with a fresh tray, friend. There's ALWAYS one more plate to fill.
Then Paul draws a line: from now on, nobody should cause him trouble. That's Paul putting his whole life on Do Not Disturb.

cards.question: Paul points to his own body as the reason no one should cause him trouble. What does he say about it?

answers.text: He bears the marks of Jesus on his body
He has grown too old to keep traveling
He has fasted for forty days and nights

cards.text: And Paul signs off with one last blessing for his brothers.

cards.question: Paul boasts only in the cross of Jesus, not in circumcision. In his final blessing, what does he pray will be with the Galatians' spirit?

answers.text: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ
The careful keeping of the law

cards.text: Then he seals it with one word: "Amen." Now THAT'S how you close a letter, friend, not with "Sent from my phone."

findings.problem: Verse 11's detail about Paul's large letters is never actually taught. Card 1 mentions only that Paul writes with his own hand, and marking the statement about tiny handwriting as False does not establish that Paul calls attention to his large letters. No later card supplies that detail.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: This asks for the unseen next word of Paul's line in verse 15. Neither card 10 nor the earlier cards give the baker a basis to reason out "creation" rather than "tradition" or "promise," so the blank tests wording rather than informed meaning.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentences: the statement about peace and mercy, the fresh-tray comparison, and the line about one more plate. Non-opening story cards are limited to two sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
